title: Dual-propagation for WebSocket + gRPC with backpressure-aware tracing hooks
creator: Noah Chen
description: Implement a dual-path context propagation layer and lightweight tracing hooks that work consistently across WebSocket streaming and gRPC streaming transports. Goal: preserve W3C traceparent and baggage, avoid trace fan-out under heavy streaming/backpressure, and provide SDK/middleware primitives for automatic header/frame enrichment and safe async span linking. This ticket covers design, runtime adapters, integration tests, and a small set of perf/latency dashboards to validate behavior.
acceptance_criteria: W3C traceparent and baggage are preserved end-to-end for request/response flows over both WebSocket and gRPC streaming in the SDKs
When streams are under high backpressure, tracing hooks do not create more than 5% additional request throughput latency at p95 compared to baseline
Sampling decision is consistent across transport handoffs: initial sampling decision is attached to the trace carrier and honored by downstream services
No unbounded memory growth in instrumentation layer during long-lived streams (validated by unit + long-run integration tests)
Automated integration test covers context restoration after reconnect/resume (WebSocket) and server-stream restarts (gRPC)
Design doc and SDK API proposal reviewed and approved by Observability and Platform teams, and PR merged with e2e tests
comments: 2026-03-01 - Noah Chen: Initial spike completed. Prototype shim implemented in the Node SDK that attaches W3C traceparent to both WebSocket frames (x-redwood-trace header in the initial handshake + per-frame lightweight tag) and gRPC metadata. Observed header size growth; moved baggage into separate compressed carrier header (x-redwood-baggage-zip).

2026-03-03 - Priya Singh: Reviewed prototype. Concern: per-frame span creation caused excessive CPU on high-throughput message buses. Proposal: switch to span-linking model where a parent stream span is created and individual messages attach link references instead of full spans. Sketch added to design doc.

2026-03-04 - Marco Alvarez (Observability): Added perf test plan. We should measure p50/p95/p99 latency delta at 10k msg/s with three message sizes. Also capture heap profile for the instrumentation layer during sustained 30m run.

2026-03-06 - Priya Singh: Implemented backpressure-aware sampling: when the transport reports write buffer saturation > 70%, span emission is throttled and a sample-count metric is incremented. This avoids trace explosion while preserving representative sampling. Added metric: obs.traces.throttled_count and obs.traces.throttle_ratio.

2026-03-08 - Design review outcome: Observability and Platform approved link-based model and compressed carrier header. Action items: add explicit reconnection logic tests for WebSocket (resume token carrying trace carrier) and add compatibility adapter for older clients still sending x-redwood-ctx.

2026-03-09 - QA: Integration tests green for Node and Python SDKs except one flaky case where gRPC stream reconnect lost baggage after a retry. Root cause: retry path was bypassing metadata re-attachment. Patch in review (PR #4582).

2026-03-10 - Priya Singh: Created Grafana dashboard panels for streaming trace throughput, obs.traces.throttled_count, and gRPC metadata reattach failure rate. Initial run shows throttle events correlate with increases in queue depth during load test.

2026-03-10 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Reviewed header compression approach. Note: ensure compressed carrier is integrity-protected and not used as a place to leak secrets. Added checklist to design doc for HMAC/signing when using compressed carriers over untrusted networks.
implementation_notes: SDK surface: provide middleware that can be registered for both HTTP/gRPC and WebSocket transports; default to W3C traceparent + compressed baggage header (x-redwood-bagg) if baggage > 512 bytes
Runtime shim: provide non-blocking hook points that can be no-op when user opts out to keep overhead minimal
Backpressure hook: transport layer must expose an interface to report output buffer fill percentage; tracer subscribes and adjusts span emission rate
Testing: add long-run integration job (30m) that simulates intermittent reconnects and bursty traffic; assert memory stable and sampling ratios within expected band
Compatibility: adapter layer to translate legacy x-redwood-ctx -> traceparent + baggage on ingress for older clients
next_steps: Merge PR #4582 after addressing gRPC reconnect baggage bug
Finish Python SDK adapter and run cross-language end-to-end test harness
Widen load tests to include Dedicated clusters and Private deployment to validate carrier integrity behind VPC/NG proxies
Add alert on obs.traces.throttle_ratio > 0.2 sustained for 5m to catch unexpected trace loss
